title: Recover orphaned fetched carriers without blocking later exchanges
outcome: An abandoned fetched carrier has an explicit audited recovery that preserves custody and uncertainty while allowing later exchanges.
acceptance: A data-branch operation whose carrier commit selection was retained by fetch but whose request never reaches the exchange ledger has a supported, audited recovery that allows later exchanges, without loosening the custody guard, rewinding Git or deleting private files by hand.

A Windows behavioral regression retains a fetched operation, leaves it without a ledger outcome through a pre-ledger refusal other than head change, proves a later exchange is initially refused by custody, and proves it is admitted after the supported recovery.

Recovery proves the exact repository, binding and retained operation it accounts for, refuses contradictory canonical progress or uncertain publication/live execution authority, and preserves unrelated retained operations and original canonical bytes.
